imported_summary_unverified:
At height p-1, the Ravenel p-cell alpha_1 complex gives the requested p-stage filtration of E_{p-1} by suspended copies of E_{p-1}^{hC_p}. For every cyclic stabilizer subgroup C_{p^n}, a theorem of Meier--Naumann--Noel gives a stable-multiple analogue: some finite wedge E_h^{\vee q} has an exact qp^n-stage filtration by suspended copies of E_h^{hC_{p^n}}. A rank-one external filtration is equivalent to realizing the regular residual representation k[C_{p^n}], while Carrick's chromatic-defect computation implies that every external T(r)-free Wood witness at height (p-1)p^{n-1}m must satisfy r at least p^{n-1}m; hence the height-p-1 alpha_1 complex cannot simply be reused outside n=m=1.

Candidate contribution (obstruction_and_reduction; novelty confidence low): For h=(p-1)p^{n-1}m and H=C_{p^n}, some E_h^{\vee q} has an exact qp^n-stage E_h^{hH}-cell filtration, whereas every external T(r)-free Wood witness has r at least p^{n-1}m; moreover, a p^n-cell rank-one candidate is reduced to the test (g-1)^{p^n-1} nonzero on its Morava K-cohomology.
